name: Two Point Museum VR
tagline: Your museum as a living model on the table in front of you.
description:
Two Point Museum VR puts your whole museum on a table in front of you, like a model you can pick up. Grab it to move it, pull your hands apart to zoom in on a single exhibit, and twist to turn it round. Guests wander the halls, staff get on with their jobs, and you build and run everything as usual.

Your hand is the mouse: point the laser at the game's menus and click, pick exhibits up and put them down where you like. The game's menus float on a panel behind the table, or split into windows around it, and you can move them wherever suits you. Prefer a smaller view? Turntable shows a circle of the museum on a table that spins.
requirements: Runs in DirectX 11. The installer sets the launch options for you.
Made for seated play: the table sits at 0.75 m by default, and you can raise it on the View page.
Tested on a Quest 2 through SteamVR. Other SteamVR headsets should work but haven't been tested.
Left-handed players can swap the laser to the left hand in the VR menu.
firstLaunch: It takes a few minutes, with a blank window, while BepInEx reads the game. It needs the internet that first time. Keep your VPN off.
needToKnow: The game's camera tutorial asks you to tilt the camera: click the right stick. The table itself doesn't tilt, so lean or move your head to see it from another angle. While you're holding an exhibit, the same click changes placement mode instead.

controls.action: Click. Hold on an exhibit to pick it up, let go to put it down
Pan around the museum (in Turntable, move the circle)
Tilt the game's camera (the table itself doesn't tilt). While holding an exhibit, change placement mode

controls.input: A, or right stick left / right

controls.action: Open or close the VR menu
Open the VR menu, at any time

tutorial.title: Getting started
tutorial.text: Load a save as usual. The museum appears as a diorama on a table in front of you. The game's menus float on a panel behind it. Open the VR menu to move it, or to split it into windows on the Game UI page.

tutorial.title: Point, click and pick up
tutorial.text: Your right hand is a laser pointer, like the mouse. These controls are for right-handed play: Left-handed (in the settings here, or on the VR menu's Controls page) swaps the hands.
controls: A, or right stick left / right

controls.action: Change placement mode while holding one
Tilt the game's camera (the table itself doesn't tilt)

tutorial.title: Diorama or Turntable
tutorial.text: Pick the view on the VR menu's View page. Diorama puts the whole museum on the table; Turntable shows a circle of it on a table that spins. The table sits at 0.75 m for seated play: change its height on the View page, or grip it and lift or lower it.

tutorial.title: The VR menu
tutorial.text: Settings, the controls (you can rebind them) and where the game's windows sit are all in the VR menu. Its Help page answers questions about Two Point Museum in VR.

tutorial.title: The game's camera tutorial
tutorial.text: It asks for keys you don't have in VR. The Tutorial button bar by the table has them: arrows to pan, turn, zoom and tilt. Point the laser at one and pull the trigger. Switch the bar on or off on the VR menu's Home page. When it asks you to tilt the camera, click the right stick.

tutorial.title: If something goes wrong
tutorial.text: The first start takes a few minutes with a blank window; leave it be. If it crashes or looks wrong, the file BepInEx\LogOutput.log in the game folder says why. Uninstalling here puts the game back to normal, and your saves are never touched.

options.label: Keep the monitor view
options.help: Draw the game on the monitor too while you're in VR. Costs frame rate.
